title: Constrain AnalyticsService.logEvent to the AnalyticsEvent catalog — LogEvents-sourced calls leak profile_id and content identifiers to Firebase Analytics

evidence.quote: // Typed string constants for structured log event names.

why: AnalyticsService.logEvent(String name, ...) accepts any bare string, so nothing stops a caller from importing LogEvents — documented in its own header as 'structured log event names' for AppLogger, not an analytics catalog — and piping it straight into real Firebase Analytics. Grepping every `.logEvent(` call site in lib/ shows ~15 places do exactly this, bypassing the audited 12-event AnalyticsEvent catalog and its PV-1 review entirely. At least 7 of those sites attach identifying data: outbox_processor.dart fires sync_outbox_dead_lettered with entity_key = '${profileId}:${sefariaRef}:${stageId}:${trackType}:${curriculumId}' (confirmed composition in completion_writer.dart:747) for every dead-lettered completion row — combining the per-child profile id with the exact Torah/Mishnah reference the child was studying in one string; pull_pipeline.dart fires sync_merge_router_halt with a bare profile_id; tutor_pin_service.dart fires tutor_pin_set with a bare profile_id; tutor_audit_log_writer.dart fires tutor_action_recorded with a 'target' field whose own documented shape is a resource path like 'profile/42.displayName' (line 130) — i.e. the profile id again, now attached to a description of what was changed; sync_orchestrator.dart fires sync_pull_failed and sync_listener_error with the raw exception's `.toString()`, which for Firestore permission/not-found errors routinely embeds the full document resource path (profiles/{id}/completions/{ref}). In release/profile builds analyticsServiceProvider resolves to the real FirebaseAnalyticsService (analytics_provider.dart), whose logEvent forwards `parameters` verbatim with zero redaction (firebase_analytics_service.dart:29-32) — so every one of these fires a real event to Google's servers. This is materially worse than the two baselined single-field leaks (bare sefaria_ref, bare profile_id in analytics_service.dart) because several of these sites combine per-child identity with content/action detail in one uncatalogued, unreviewed string, and remains a live COPPA/GDPR-K risk independent of the separately-baselined PV-3 consent-gating gap (fixing consent gating controls whether these fire at all, not what's inside them once a user has consented).
recommendation: Change AnalyticsService.logEvent's name parameter from bare String to a closed type sourced only from AnalyticsEvent (e.g. an extension type/sealed wrapper), add a Rule-0 grep/lint that fails CI on any `.logEvent(` call whose first argument isn't `AnalyticsEvent.<x>`, and triage the 7 cited sites: either drop the identifying parameter and keep these as AppLogger-only structured logs (most already have a parallel LogEvents-based AppLogger call right next to the analytics one), or promote them into AnalyticsEvent with PV-1-safe parameters (counts/enums/booleans only) and route error detail through a stable EH-5 error-code enum instead of `.toString()`.
acceptance_criteria: A checker (grep in make audit, or a working custom_lint rule) fails with file:line on any AnalyticsService.logEvent(...)/.logEvent( call whose event-name argument is not an AnalyticsEvent member
entity_key/profile_id/target/error-text parameters are removed, hashed, or replaced with a coarse enum at all 7 cited call sites

A regression test asserts FakeAnalyticsService-captured params for outbox_dead_lettered, merge_router_halt, pull_failed, listener_error, tutor_pin_set, and tutor_action_recorded never contain a raw profileId, sefariaRef, or exception string
docs/coding-standards.md PV-1 known-gaps list is either cleared for these sites or explicitly extended to name them

corrections: TutorAuditLogWriter (tutor_audit_log_writer.dart, the 7th site, 'target'/'grant_id' leak) has no constructor call anywhere in lib/ or test/ — it is currently dead/unwired code, not reachable in production today. The finding's 'sites: 7' should read 6 confirmed-reachable + 1 dormant; this does not change the verdict or severity since 6 live production leak sites remain independently confirmed, including one (entity_key) that combines profile_id with content identifier in a single string.

mergedFrom: privacy-policy.md falsely claims no analytics/crash-report collection while release builds ship FirebaseAnalyticsService + unconditional Crashlytics
Strip row.entityKey out of the outbox dead-letter analytics event (leaks profileId + sefariaRef)
Strip profile_id / child_profile_id from tutor_pin_service.dart and tutor_invite_use_cases.dart analytics events
